title: Skyloom
tagline: Weave the sky. Land them all.
teaser: Jets and props pour into your airspace. Draw their routes through beacons, stack their altitudes, and thread them onto the runway in a perfect string of lights. Born on Berkeley terminals in 1986 — now with a sky you can tilt.

inspiredBy.uiTitle: the 1986 Berkeley air traffic control game

manPage.synopsis: skyloom — weave routes through a busy sky; land every plane and send the rest out at 9 000 ft.
manPage.description: Ed James wrote atc at UC Berkeley in 1986–87, working, as its manual cheerfully admits, from a secondhand account of an older PC game. Skyloom keeps its tick-by-tick rules exactly and lets you draw routes, see conflicts coming, tilt the radar to read altitude, and fly a campaign, an endless ladder and a shared daily sky.

howToPlay: Drag from a plane to draw its route through beacons to its gate or runway.
Keep every pair more than a cell apart, or two thousand feet; the ring warns you ticks ahead.
Land at 0 ft along the runway, leave at 9 000 ft through the right gate.
